chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyam, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with his wife before he performed the Tawaf al-Nisa' (Women's Circumambulation), and he said: 'Upon him is a fat camel, and if he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him.'

He said: And I asked him about a man who kissed his wife, and he had performed Tawaf al-Nisa', but she had not performed it, and he said: 'Upon him is blood (damm) which he must shed from his own side.'

If he had performed from the Tawaf al-Nisa' that which exceeds half, he builds upon it when he performs Ghusl, and if he had not reached half, then upon him is the re-performance of the circumambulation.

key_terms.جَزُورٌ سَمِينَةٌ: A fat camel, a specific type of animal sacrifice used as expiation
key_terms.دَمٌ: Damm, a specific expiation involving shedding blood, often by sacrificing an animal
key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa', the final circumambulation of the Kaaba performed to complete Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man who has intercourse with his wife before completing Tawaf al-Nisa' during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific financial expiations (kaffarah) for pilgrims who engage in marital relations during Hajj, distinguishing between ignorance and deliberate violation. It establishes that pre-Tawaf al-Nisa' intercourse incurs the penalty of a fat camel (jazoor), while post-Tawaf al-Nisa' intercourse by the husband while the wife remains uncompleted requires shedding blood (damm), reflecting the juristic emphasis on the sequential validity of the Tawaf pillars. The ruling also provides practical guidance on partial completion, requiring re-circumambulation if less than half is completed, thereby ensuring the ritual's integrity.
